{"self_assessment": "Impact: My contribution was quality assurance. I inspected the chain three times (early body, mid-build, and the tail join), and each time I reported what I found to the table. My checks confirmed the run carried from the start through nearly all of the 110 dominoes, which gave the table the confidence to stop adding things and lock the design in. I did not lay dominoes or draw on the pad, so my impact comes from verification, not construction.

Execution: I timed my inspections to the riskiest moments: the body as it grew, the tail curves, and the final join near the belly end. I traced the fall by eye from the start and reported the result: it carried all the way round, with one small stray by the dip that was left alone to avoid risking the top line. After that I stayed hands-off so there was no chance of a bump knocking down a run, which matters when two people working within a few units of each other can cause one.

Collaboration: I backed the table's calls on the fish, the rounded tail and the single-line join, and I offered to take the lower half of the tail or patch gaps if needed. I gave my teammates clear confirmations and credited their work openly. I also held off on the join when Sofia asked, so we didn't double up on it.

Leadership: I did not direct the build. The fish concept, the sketch and the tail redesign were driven by others. My leadership was in keeping the table calm and aligned at the end: confirming the chain was sound, encouraging a hands-off finish, and keeping the mood positive through the final two minutes. I would aim to take a more active building or coordinating role next time.", "my_share_percent": 10}
